notes: Official ADLIA version of the 1997 Labour Code lists amendments through 22 Jul 2013 and states that code was repealed by the 2016 Labour Code. No 2015 annual-leave amendment was identified. Treat the EW2015 21→18 working-day jump as a measurement/coding discontinuity unless contrary legal evidence is found.

Older law reported a minimum of 18 working days. ILO EPLex records Labour Law Act No.49/08 amended by Act No.59/2011 of 14 Dec 2011; by the later screening period the statutory floor was 20 working days. The World Bank EW2010 +1 jump does not align to a clean legal event, and the 2011 amendment was broad.

The consolidated Labour Law was already in force with at least 20 working days by this period. No 2015 annual-leave entitlement decrease matching the EW2015 -0.33 average jump was identified. Treat as panel coding/tenure-profile movement, not a reform.

NATLEX's Labour Code amendment history shows the 2012 labour-rights law and then later amendments, but no 2013 annual-leave reform. The 2012 law focused on enforcement, social-security affiliation, lactation and domestic-worker rest; the statutory annual vacation rule remains 15 days. The EW2013 -0.33 jump is not a verified leave reform.
